official_measurement_examples.name: WRMP strategic scale
official_measurement_examples.fact: Water companies must prepare and maintain WRMPs describing how they will secure supplies and protect the environment; the plans operate at company and water-resource-zone scale rather than proving a connection is available for a specific parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 planning guideline timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Water Resources Planning Guideline was updated 16 June 2026 and sets the WRMP29 preparation timetable, including pre-consultation from 2026 and later draft/final plan milestones.

official_measurement_examples.name: Water Resource Zone limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The January 2026 Water Resource Zones dataset maps water-company supply operating boundaries; a polygon match identifies the resource-zone geography but not spare network or treatment capacity at a development site.

official_measurement_examples.name: Supply-demand forecast scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency WRMP forecast data provides supply-demand information at water-company and resource-zone scale from 2025 to at least 2050 and must not be downscaled into unsupported parcel capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: DWMP hierarchy
official_measurement_examples.fact: Statutory DWMP guidance uses company, catchment/local-authority and sewerage-catchment planning levels and requires consideration of current and future capacity and resilience; it is not a site-specific sewer-connection approval.

official_measurement_examples.name: Preferred option limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Framework WRMP24 option data records preferred future supply and transfer options and their expected Ml/d contribution; an option in a preferred plan is not evidence that capacity is already delivered at a parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Demand target distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 water-demand target plan sets national per-capita and leakage targets; those targets do not themselves determine local development water availability.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current water situation distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency monthly water-situation reports describe rainfall, soil moisture, river flow, groundwater and reservoir conditions and should not be used as a substitute for statutory network-capacity or connection evidence.

core_rules: WRMP company or resource-zone forecasts are not parcel connection approvals
Water Resource Zone boundaries identify operating geography not spare capacity
DWMP catchment planning is not evidence of site-specific sewer capacity
a preferred future water-resource option is not delivered capacity
national water-demand targets are not parcel capacity measurements
monthly hydrological status is not a water-company connection decision
planning permission is distinct from water and sewer connection approval
strategic water supply evidence must retain forecast year and scenario
strategic wastewater evidence must retain company catchment and planning level
future planned infrastructure must not be represented as operational today
supply-demand surplus or deficit at zone scale must not be silently downscaled to a parcel
environmental abstraction constraints are distinct from distribution-network capacity
water-company duties do not determine land ownership or access rights
water/wastewater planning evidence does not reserve development capacity
no parcel water-capacity clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
